title: VA Home Loan Guaranty Partial Claim Terms by Program
content:
A VA partial claim under the VA Home Loan Guaranty is the amount VA pays a servicer to bring a defaulted loan current, owed back by the veteran as a subordinate lien. Each program sets the partial claim ceiling (the largest partial claim, as a percent of the unpaid principal balance at the first unpaid installment), the annual interest the partial claim bears, whether it falls due when the first mortgage is paid off, refinanced or the property sold, and the number of missed monthly payments a borrower must have before a partial claim is offered.

## Terms by program

| Program | Partial claim ceiling (% of unpaid principal balance at the first unpaid installment) | Partial claim interest (% a year) | Due on payoff, refinance or sale | Missed monthly payments required |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| VA Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loan (IRRRL) | 30 | 1.0 | Yes | 2 |
| VA Manufactured Home Loan | 30 | 1.0 | Yes | 2 |
| VA Purchase Loan (10% or More Down) | 30 | 1.0 | Yes | 2 |
| VA Purchase Loan (5% to Less Than 10% Down) | 30 | 1.0 | Yes | 2 |
| VA Purchase Loan (Less Than 5% Down) | 30 | 1.0 | Yes | 2 |
| VA Cash-Out Refinance Loan | 30 | 1.0 | Yes | 2 |
| Native American Direct Loan (NADL) | 30 | 1.0 | Yes | 2 |

## Points of reading

- The ceiling is measured on the unpaid principal balance at the first unpaid installment, not on the original loan amount.
- The required missed payments are a floor: a borrower with 2 or more missed monthly payments meets it, a borrower with 1 does not.

## Hypothetical illustration

On a hypothetical unpaid principal balance of 180,000.00 dollars at the first unpaid installment, 30 percent is 180,000.00 multiplied by 30 and divided by one hundred, or 54,000.00 dollars.
